notes: 2018_00_link is an HR leave summary (undated; footer Sep 25 2017); 2018_03 is OP 70.44 (9/24/14); 2018_04 is an excerpt of OP 70.32 (10/12/17); 2018_01 is the 2017-18 Faculty Handbook, whose governing passages are MIDP, benefits, OP 32.01 and OP 32.11.

Governing documents: OP 70.32 (10/12/17 edition, 2018_04) for FMLA and state parental leave; OP 32.11 (9/12/06) and OP 70.44 (9/24/14) for sick leave and the pool; OP 32.01 (7/11/12) for the probationary period; the Faculty Handbook text for MIDP and STD/LTD. The handbook's own copy of OP 70.32 is the superseded 2/5/14 edition (it said 'Texas Tech allows the use of sick leave' and barred intermittent leave after a birth); the 10/12/17 edition governs on 2018-02-28 and is coded.

No paid parental, maternity or childbirth leave, and no employer-paid FMLA, appears in any source. Pay during a birth comes only from the member's own sick leave (and vacation for 12-month faculty), then the sick leave pool only for catastrophic complications; the rest of FMLA is leave without pay. OP 70.44 5.c: 'Time off following the birth of a child is considered normal regardless of the method of delivery'.

U8: OP 70.32 §10 state parental leave (Tex. Gov't Code 661.913; up to 12 workweeks for employees with under 12 months or 1,250 hours) is recorded in c1's note, not as a component; the two-year member is FMLA-eligible.

Documents cited but not saved: OP 32.35 Modified Instructional Duties Policy (governs c7: eligibility, length, approval and pay unknown); OP 70.43 Leave Without Pay; OP 70.45 Vacation Leave (and holiday leave); OP 70.39 early return-to-work, alternate and light duty assignments; OP 70.04 Military Emergency Leave; OP 70.05; OP 32.34; the Tex. Gov't Code ch. 661 sections (661.912, 661.913 etc.) are not saved; ERS plan documents for STD/LTD (www.ers.state.tx.us). The handbook's communicable-disease paragraph mentions 'temporary disability leave without pay benefits in accordance with normal university policies (OP 70.01)', but OP 70.01 (saved) contains no such leave; no terms, so not coded.

Conflict: the faculty sick leave pool cap in OP 32.11 §5.c (2006: 'lesser of one-third of the total amount of time in the pool or 90 days') differs from OP 70.44 §5 (2014: service bands, 1,440 hours per employment); OP 70.44, the later and specific pool policy to which OP 70.01 refers, is coded (c4 flagged conflicting_sources).

Faculty development leave (OP 32.29; Tex. Educ. Code 51.102-51.108: one semester at full pay or a year at half pay for tenured faculty with five years of service, for study and research) and OP 70.01 miscellaneous leaves (emergency, funeral, jury, military, donor, foster-parent meetings, parent-teacher conferences) are not usable for a birth and are not components (checklist §1).

Most faculty hold 9-month appointments ('Faculty on nine-month appointments (most all faculty)'); vacation (c3) accrues only to 12-month appointees and is recorded by that group. For 9-month faculty FML is charged only during duty periods (OP 70.32 §17).

Chain, birth parent: FMLA 12 workweeks (c1) from the birth, with own sick leave (c2, and vacation c3 for 12-month faculty only) paid within it, then the sick leave pool (c4) only for catastrophic complications after sick leave, then leave without pay to the end of the 12 weeks.
Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA 12 workweeks (c1) from the birth, with own sick leave usable for the birth under FMLA (c2) within it, then leave without pay; no other parental provision.

General-purpose provisions recorded but counted nowhere: MIDP (c7; open list of significant life events), leave without pay (c8, HR summary only), tenure-clock extension for extenuating circumstances (c9), vacation (c3).
